thread:
Maria: heads-up — noticed a mismatch between the billing cohorts dashboard and sampled traces this morning. some high-volume tenants show lower sample coverage than expected, which skews cost attributions.
Aj: ugh. is this the post-enrich sampling path again?
Maria: looks like it. we retried a backfill and the sample rate computed after enrichment diverged from the ingress sampler for a few tenants.
Samir: can you paste an example?
Maria: sure. here’s a minimal snippet from the trace header we saw: ```json
{"tenant_id":"acme","route":"generate","ingress_sample":0.1,"post_enrich_sample":0.03,"billing_cohort":"gen-tier-b"}
```
Aj: ok that explains it — billing_cohort is derived in enrichment, so if we naively sample post-enrich we change the cohort distribution.
Samir: two obvious choices: 1) deterministically sample at ingress using a key that hashes to the eventual billing cohort (if we can predict it), or 2) always propagate an ingress_sample_key and use that for billing/hashing later.
Maria: 2) seems safer for unpredicatable cohort derivation. we already propagate a trace_id and tenant_id, but cohort depends on prompt size & routing.
Aj: downside of option 2 is that we keep more metadata in-flight and it increases header size. also late-joiners/edge proxies might drop it.
Samir: thought: introduce a small stable token 'sample_key' at ingress: compute hash(sample_key) -> sample_decision and also attach sample_key to the envelope. downstream enrichment computes billing_cohort but uses sample_key to attribute to cohort consistently.
Maria: that would keep sampling decisions stable without needing to recompute. also would allow us to recompute cohort buckets in analytics by joining on sample_key.
Aj: how does this affect backfills? if someone reruns enrichment on old traces, they need sample_key present or we'll shift counts.
Samir: we should forbid retroactive cohorting changes for already-sampled items. add a migration policy: if sample_key missing, fall back to best-effort cohort mapping but mark the record as 'cohort_approx'.
Maria: implementation concerns: upstream SDKs + edge proxies need to set sample_key. we could default to trace_id for existing clients to avoid rollout explosion, but prefer explicit sample_key to decouple from trace_id churn.
Aj: also consider reservoir sampling for ultra-high-cardinality tenants: keep a reservoir per billing_cohort_shard keyed by sample_key%N so we don't over-index any single tenant.
Maria: open question: should billing pipelines trust post-enrich cohort or the ingress-derived cohort? we want the single source of truth to be the cohort computed post-enrich, but sampling alignment must not change attribution.
Samir: proposed compromise: cohort = post-enrich computation, attribution uses (sample_key -> cohort) mapping emitted at enrich time into a small mapping table. billing pipeline reads mapping table to map sampled trace -> cohort.
Aj: sounds good. can we put an RFC together with migration/playback plan and perf impact (header size, storage for mapping table)?
Maria: yes. I'll draft RFC and include a rollout plan: stage 1 - propagate sample_key in SDKs; stage 2 - enrich writes sample_key->cohort mapping to compact store; stage 3 - billing pipeline reads mapping; stage 4 - backfill helpers for missing sample_key marked as cohort_approx.
infra-bot: created ticket INF-7421: "sample_key propagation + cohort mapping for stable cost attribution" -> https://go/internal/INF-7421
Aj: cheers. assign to Samir + Maria for the first draft. I'll add perf estimates for header/ingest overhead.
Samir: will start a short spike tomorrow to validate collision/entropy of sample_key derived from trace_id vs random UUID.
Maria: thanks — circle back once the RFC is up. :thumbsup:
